data.narrative:
Locus Robotics, a Series F robotics and manufacturing company, carries a current post-money valuation of $2.0B following $438M in total capital raised across its founders Bruce Welty, Rick Faulk, and Al Dekin. The valuation assessment draws from a comp universe of 9 peers: 1 public company and 8 private robotics firms spanning stages from Series B through Series E, including Divergent ($2.3B), Exotec ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), Dexterity ($1.6B), and Hadrian ($1.6B).

Two methods triangulate the valuation. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.3x step-up multiplier typical of Series F advancement to the $2.0B base, yielding $2.6B. Peer-median valuation across 7 same-sector comparables with similar valuation tiers produces $1.6B, with the peer set ranging from $1.0B to $2.3B. These methods reflect differing assumptions: stage-progression assumes above-median progression velocity, while peer-median anchors to realized market pricing across the ecosystem.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.4B (25th percentile) to $3.0B (75th percentile), with a median of $2.1B. The current $2.0B valuation sits near the low end of this range. Key uncertainties include the relative weighting of near-term financing momentum versus peer-set reversion, and stage-specific valuation inflection patterns within the robotics sector.
